answer: A cold-hour ember relay makes seats costly to clone. Each seat binds to a numbered cairn on a named mesa: at the nadir of an assigned night the holder must carry a live ember from the hearth to the cairn, where a keeper stamps arrival and photographs coal hot enough to light tinder. One journey buys one seat-day. A thousand cloned wallets cannot fake that: each extra identity needs its own courier, coal and countersign, and the coal must still glow on arrival, so it cannot be pre-filmed. The thousandth fake agent costs what the first did, a night of labour plus a fee, never amortizing.
